newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSIGHT - JGBs seen set to fall on rate rise report.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - JGBs seen set to fall on rate rise report.

text.p: Cash and futures JGBs are seen set to ease on Tuesday on an early morning television report that Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) will make a recommendation to Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto by the end of this month that Japan raise its official discount rate.

NHK television reported on Tuesday that an LDP administrative reform panel will make the recommendation in light of parliamentary passage of a bill to drastically reform Japan's Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Control Law.
It did not say what the extent of the rate rise recommended by the LDP would be.
LDP officials were not immediately available to confirm the NHK report. The new foreign exchange law goes into effect on April 1 next year.

The LDP panel argued that Japan needs to raise interest rates to avoid further capital outflows from Japan because the new forex law could further push Japanese capital out of Tokyo into higher-yielding foreign securities markets.
Traders said the June futures contract's support at 123.50 and 123.00 could easily be broken after the report.
